decisions.thought: Plan: Lead Incineroar for Fake Out and Intimidate, with Garchomp as the mega threat. Gholdengo gives special power for the Steel/Ghost matchups. The opponent has Dragonite, Garchomp, Gholdengo, Rotom-Wash, Kingambit and Skeledirge. Watch for Gholdengo's Good as Gold and Rotom-Wash's Levitate. Expect Dragon and Ground attacks against Garchomp.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm weighing team composition against their Dragon-heavy core of Dragonite and Garchomp, leaning toward Corviknight for broad matchup coverage and Incineroar as a lead with Fake Out and Intimidate.

After weighing coverage against Rotom-Wash, Kingambit, and Skeledirge, I'll settle on Incineroar, Garchomp, and Gholdengo for a balance of offensive pressure and solid resistances.

decisions.thought: Lead Garchomp: set Stealth Rock, Focus Sash guarantees a move; Earthquake/Scale Shot pressure Incineroar, Kingambit, Gholdengo. Gholdengo blocks their hazards removal and hits Corviknight/Sinistcha. Dragonite with Multiscale + Dragon Dance is the late-game cleaner; watch for opposing Garchomp (Ice Spinner covers it).
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Pick Garchomp lead (rocks, sash), Gholdengo, Dragonite.

decisions.thought: Lead Incineroar vs their Garchomp (-1 Atk from Intimidate). Fake Out now: it's priority, we outspeed, and it flinches. Expect Garchomp to hit hard next turn (Earthquake/Dragon Claw). Plan: Gholdengo or Garchomp handles Garchomp later. Watch for Rotom-Wash (Levitate, immune to Ground). Their pool: Dragonite, Gholdengo, Rotom-Wash, Kingambit, Skeledirge. Garchomp may have Rough Skin (contact costs us 1/8 HP).
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Fake Out seems like the right opening move here since it guarantees free damage and a flinch on Garchomp, moving first thanks to priority, even accounting for possible Rough Skin recoil.

decisions.thought: Lead Garchomp vs Incineroar (Intimidate, Atk -1). Plan: Earthquake now—super effective even at -1; they may switch to Garchomp/Kingambit. Keep Sash intact for later rocks if forced out. Dragonite cleans late; Gholdengo walls their Gholdengo/Sinistcha.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Earthquake at -1 still hits hard; Incineroar likely switches or uses Knock Off. Set rocks? EQ is super effective and they may stay. I'll EQ.

decisions.thought: Opponent Garchomp (84%, Atk -1) has Rough Skin, so contact hurts us. Parting Shot cuts its Atk and SpA and pivots Incineroar out. Our Garchomp (garchompite) comes in next, and I plan to Mega it once it's safe. Watch for Dragonite, Gholdengo, Rotom-Wash (Levitate), Kingambit and Skeledirge. Gholdengo is weak to Ground, so keep it away from their Garchomp's Earthquake.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar's at 177/202 against the opposing Garchomp at 84% with a -1 Attack drop, and I'm checking whether the opposing Garchomp has its mega stone - mine does, so I could mega evolve mine next turn. I'm weighing whether to switch into my Garchomp now, since Incineroar wouldn't take damage on the switch but my Garchomp would eat a hit from the opposing one.

Flare Blitz from Incineroar would only do neutral or resisted damage against Garchomp's Dragon/Ground typing, so that's not ideal. I'm leaning toward Parting Shot instead - it weakens Garchomp's offenses while letting me bring in Gholdengo safely, though I need to check how Gholdengo's Steel/Ghost typing interacts with an incoming Earthquake.

Actually, pivoting into my own Garchomp looks stronger: Parting Shot further cripples their Garchomp's Attack, and my Garchomp can tank the Ground-type hit before setting up with Swords Dance or mega evolving next turn.

Earthquake hits both ways, though Rough Skin chips us on contact. Overall our Garchomp is the better pick here—faster and not too exposed to Ground. Going with Garchomp.
